section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Nature of Light Waves
section_1.content: Introduce light as a wave. Explain that light travels at a constant speed (c) in a vacuum, but slows down when entering denser materials. Use the concept of 'Optical Density' to establish that speed determines the path.
section_1.example: Imagine a marching band transitioning from a smooth pavement to deep mud; the side that hits the mud first slows down, causing the whole line to turn.

section_2.title: Defining Refraction and Snell's Law
section_2.content: Define refraction as the bending of light at the boundary of two media. Present Snell's Law: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2). Represent this visually with a ray diagram showing the angle of incidence vs. the angle of refraction relative to the 'normal' line.
section_2.example: A laser pointer beam hitting a glass block at an angle, showing how the light 'bends' toward the normal when entering the denser medium.

section_3.title: Visualizing Optical Density (The 'N' Factor)
section_3.content: Explain the Refractive Index (n). A higher 'n' means the medium is optically 'slower'. Use a split-screen animation: one side shows light in air (n=1), the other in water (n=1.33) or diamond (n=2.4), illustrating varying degrees of bending.
section_3.example: A visual comparison: A straw in a glass of water appears 'broken' because the brain traces the refracted light rays backward in a straight line.

section_4.title: Real-World Application: The Archer Fish
section_4.content: Synthesize the knowledge: How do animals adapt? Explain that the Archer Fish must aim 'below' the perceived image of its prey because of refraction, adjusting its angle based on the known refractive index of water.
section_4.example: An animation of an Archer Fish calculating the 'refraction shift' to accurately spit water at a bug sitting on a leaf above the surface.

section_5.title: Summary and Concept Check
section_5.content: Recap the three core rules: 1. Speed changes at boundaries. 2. Light bends toward the normal in denser media. 3. The Refractive Index (n) quantifies this behavior. End with a quick quiz question on total internal reflection as a teaser for the next lesson.
section_5.example: A quick visual challenge: Present a fiber-optic cable and ask students to predict if light will escape the glass core, reinforcing the boundary concept.
